hint_repairs.review_required_change: All three rungs only cover a rectangle. Include the scoped branches: perimeter is twice the side-length sum; supplementary/complementary angles sum to180/90; ages use the stated age total. Combine the relevant total equation with the stated difference, solve and check both conditions and requested order.

coverage_evidence.problem: A rectangle has perimeter $34$ cm and length $3$ cm more than width. Find (length, width) in cm.
Two supplementary angles differ by $40$ degrees. Find (larger, smaller) in degrees.
Two ages sum to $38$ years; one person is $12$ years older. Find (older, younger).
A learner treats complementary angles as totaling $180$. They differ by $10$ degrees. Find the correct (larger, smaller) angles.

hints: Name the two requested quantities and choose the correct total equation: perimeter gives twice the side-length sum, supplementary or complementary angles sum to 180 or 90, and an age problem uses its stated age total.
Translate the stated difference with the larger quantity first, then solve that relationship together with the relevant total equation.
Check both original conditions and report the quantities in the order and units requested.

hint_repairs.review_required_change: Rung2 assumes the first quantity is the scaled version of the second; canonical adults/children describes the second from the first. Name both actual quantities, translate the multiplier and signed offset in the stated direction, combine with the total, solve, and check BOTH the sum and scaled relationship. Avoid people-only wording for lengths or volumes.

coverage_evidence.problem: Two numbers sum to $23$; the first is twice the second plus $2$. Find (first, second).
A group has $35$ adults and children combined; there are $3$ more than three times as many children as adults. Find (adults, children).
Two tanks total $50$ L; tank A holds $5$ L less than four times tank B. Find (A, B) volumes.
A learner multiplies the whole total by $2$ when one length is $2$ cm more than twice another and their sum is $20$ cm. Find (longer, shorter).

proposed_row.constraints: one scaled relationship plus one sum; integer answers
hints: Define variables for the two actual quantities in the requested order and write their stated total equation.
Translate the multiplier and signed offset in the direction stated, so the correct named quantity is expressed from the other.
Solve the total and scaled relationship together, then verify both equations, the integer-answer requirement, and any positivity or units required by the context; report in the requested order.

supersedes.reason: Peer review made positivity conditional on context while preserving the general integer-answer constraint.
